text:
Dr B Comber
Urologist
Southport Hospital
Gold Coast 

01 June 2010

Dear Dr Comber

Re: Mr Tom Cribb
DOB: 23/05/1982

Thank you for seeing Mr Cribb, a 28-year-old builder’s labourer who has an ectopic kidney along with hypronephrosis, for further investigation and assessment.

Mr Cribb smokes 5-6 cigarettes daily and drinks 2-5 units weekly. He has no known allergies. His mother died of breast cancer, and his father has hypertension.

Mr Cribb  presented on 12/05/2010 with acute pain in the right lower abdomen, which radiated to the groin, and nausea. However, he denied any urinary changes or associated symptoms. Examination revealed mild lower abdominal tenderness. At that time, he was diagnosed with ureteric colic, prescribed diclofenac sodium 50 mg twice daily, and advised to increase his fluid intake and to exercise regularly. 

Two days later, he was asymptomatic. An IVP revealed an ectopic, enlarged right kidney but the left kidney was normal, with no evidence of stones. Microscopic hematouria was detected by a UFR.

Today, Mr Cribb reported mild right lower abdominal pain, which responded to Panadol. A hard mass in the right lower quadrantwas found on DRE. His BP was 140/90. 
An ultrasound detected severe hydronephrosis and a liver mass. Please note, Mr Cribb will return to work in two weeks.


Kindly arrange for a CT scan as you see appropriate and assess Mr Cribb’s condition.

Should there be any queries, please do not hesitate to contact me.

Yours sincerely

Doctor.
